content: Moxifloxacin is a medication used to treat various bacterial infections. It belongs to a class of drugs known as quinolone antibiotics. This medication is effective only against bacterial infections and will not work for viral infections such as the common cold or flu. Before starting moxifloxacin, it is important to read the Medication Guide and any accompanying patient information provided by your pharmacist. Take this medication by mouth, with or without food, as directed by your doctor, usually once daily. The dosage and duration of treatment depend on your medical condition and response to therapy. Consult your pharmacist about any other products you are taking. For optimal results, take this antibiotic at evenly spaced intervals and continue the full prescribed course, even if symptoms improve after a few days. Common side effects may include nausea, diarrhea, dizziness, lightheadedness, headache, weakness, or difficulty sleeping. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. However, moxifloxacin may rarely cause a severe intestinal condition due to a bacteria called Clostridium difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or weeks to months after treatment has stopped. Prolonged or repeated use of this medication may also lead to oral thrush or a new yeast infection. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare but possible. Moxifloxacin may worsen a muscle condition called myasthenia gravis. Additionally, it can cause a condition affecting the heart rhythm known as QT prolongation, which may increase the risk of serious irregular heartbeats. The risk of QT prolongation is higher if you have certain medical conditions, take other drugs that prolong the QT interval, or have low potassium or magnesium levels in your blood. Severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting can also increase this risk. This medication may rarely cause significant changes in blood sugar levels, especially in individuals with diabetes. Monitor your blood sugar regularly and report any symptoms of high blood sugar (such as increased thirst or urination) or low blood sugar (such as sudden sweating, shaking, rapid heartbeat, hunger, blurred vision, dizziness, or tingling in the hands or feet) to your doctor. Carry glucose tablets or gel to treat low blood sugar, or use a quick source of sugar like candy, honey, fruit juice, or non-diet soda if needed. To prevent low blood sugar, eat meals on a regular schedule and avoid skipping meals. Moxifloxacin may make you feel dizzy. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can worsen this effect. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness until you can do so safely. Limit alcoholic beverages. This medication may also increase your sensitivity to sunlight. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. Live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine, may not work as effectively while you are taking moxifloxacin. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly needed, and it is unknown if it passes into breast milk. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. If someone overdoses and experiences serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. In the U.S., you can call 1-800-222-1222. Store moxifloxacin at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is less than 8 hours before your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. This medication has been prescribed for your current condition only. Do not use it later for another infection unless directed by your doctor. While taking this medication, your doctor may order lab tests, such as liver function tests, complete blood counts, or blood glucose monitoring, to check for side effects. Keep all medical and lab appointments as scheduled. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for complete information about this medication and your specific health needs.
